summary: H.R. 10908, titled the "Ending Patient Runaround Act," establishes tax-exempt Universal Savings Accounts (USAs) for health-related or personal savings with a $10,000 annual contribution limit adjusted for inflation. It also imposes new federal requirements on group health plans and health insurance issuers regarding transparency, prior authorization timelines, restrictions on changing drug tier lists or uncovered service lists, equivalent reimbursement rates for in-network and out-of-network providers, catastrophic health plan rules, dedicated points of contact for enrollees, and financial compensation penalties for billing errors.

affected_groups.effect: Can open and contribute up to $10,000 annually to tax-exempt Universal Savings Accounts.

Must comply with stricter disclosure, prior authorization deadlines, restrictions on mid-year drug tier changes, out-of-network payment parity, dedicated U.S.-based points of contact, and financial penalties for billing errors.
affected_groups.group: Group health plans and health insurance issuers

affected_groups.effect: Must participate in same-specialty peer reviews when requested, cannot be restricted by plans from serving out-of-plan individuals, and face penalties or compensation requirements for billing errors.
Gain faster prior authorization decisions, transparent pricing documentation, dedicated points of contact, and financial compensation when overbilled.

key_provisions: Creates tax-exempt Universal Savings Accounts (USAs) with an annual cash contribution limit of $10,000 per individual, indexed for inflation after 2026, allowing tax-free distributions.

Requires group health plans and health insurance issuers to issue prior authorization approvals or denials in writing through a secure portal within 30 days, and requires peer-to-peer reviews to involve a peer in the same medical specialty.
Prohibits insurers from moving prescription drugs to more restrictive tiers or changing lists of uncovered services during the term of coverage.
Requires insurers to include procedure codes, prices charged, and a full list of covered services alongside insurance contracts.
Mandates that health plans pay out-of-network providers at an amount no less than what would have been paid to a participating in-network provider.
Revises rules for basic health plans (catastrophic plans) to cover at least three primary care visits before cost-sharing applies, taking effect in 2027.

Requires health plans and providers to pay monetary compensation to enrollees for billing errors involving overcharges, ranging from 110 percent to over 150 percent of the excess charge depending on how late the refund is issued.
missing_information: Specific details regarding the exact regulatory penalties for health care providers that fail to comply with billing error compensation rules.
Detailed administrative guidance from the Secretary of the Treasury regarding the precise management and designation processes for Universal Savings Accounts.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10908, titled the "Ending Patient Runaround Act," establishes tax-exempt Universal Savings Accounts (USAs) for health-related or personal savings with a $10,000 annual contribution limit adjusted for inflation. It also imposes new federal requirements on group health plans and health insurance issuers regarding transparency, prior authorization timelines, restrictions on changing drug tier lists or uncovered service lists, equivalent reimbursement rates for in-network and out-of-network providers, catastrophic health plan rules, dedicated points of contact for enrollees, and financial compensation penalties for billing errors.
summary_detail.significance: The bill introduces sweeping changes to federal health insurance regulation, financial account structures, and consumer protections. Most provisions take effect on January 1, 2029, altering compliance standards across health plans, issuers, and providers nationwide.
